summary: Theodore Dwight Woolsey (1801–1889) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Hopkins School, Yale College, and Princeton University. He served as president of Yale University (1831–1871) and of the American Oriental Society (~1860–1866).
Theodore Gabriel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

Theodore Riccardi (1937–2023) worked in Indology and linguistics. He was a faculty member at Columbia University (attested 1974–2014) and served as guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society (attested 1989).

Theodore Stcherbatsky (1866–1942) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi, and was a member of the Imperial Academy of Sciences (attested 1927–1931).
Theodorus Willem Juynboll (1866–1948) was a scholar of religious studies and other fields. He studied at Leiden University (~1886–1893) and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.
Theophil Gubler worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel in 1903, studying under Jacob Wackernagel.

Thich Minh Chau (1918–2012) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He was a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984) and Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University.

Thich Nhat Hanh (1926–2022) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Báo Quốc Buddhist Academy, University of Saigon, Columbia, Princeton, and Princeton Theological Seminary. He taught at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh, and Cornell.
Thich Thien Chau (1931–1998) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, completing his doctoral dissertation there in 1977.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under the supervision of Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).
Thierry Mathou (born 1963) is a scholar of Tibetology and other fields. Educated at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, he has served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard (born 1963) works in Sinology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Peking University under Yulie Lou, became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006), and directed The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007), where he studied under Lewis Lancaster, Ananda Guruge, and doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya.
Thinlay Ram Shashni is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as an editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1997 and 2007).

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994), and Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School.

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche (1931–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (Dudjom Rinpoche) and founded the White Lotus School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University.

Thomas A. Tweed (born 1954) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Stanford University, where he studied under Lee Yearley and Peter N. Gregory, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at UNC Chapel Hill.
Thomas Athol Joyce (1878–1942) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Hertford College (~1897–1901) and held a post at the British Museum from circa 1902 to 1938.

Thomas B. Ellis works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).
